transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I've been having some strange moments lately. It's a bit hard to explain. 

Just... sometimes my own house, or my office, it suddenly feels unreal. Like I'm not really there. It's almost like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being in it. 

That's... that's mainly why I'm here.
How long have you been experiencing these strange, unreal moments?
About two weeks, I guess. It started... well, ever since a client threatened me in my office. Just been happening since then.
Have you experienced hearing or seeing things that aren't there during these unreal moments?
No. I haven't... no. I haven't noticed anything like that. Just what I already told you.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since the incident with your client?

I suppose so. It's just... well, even when I'm at home in Roanoke, I can't seem to just sit still. I find myself keeping track of things. Every car door that shuts outside, every footstep on the porch. 

And... I just keep checking where the exits are, wherever I am. Like I need to be ready, just in case someone comes at me again.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself or your surroundings when you're not having one of those unreal moments?
No... I don't think so. Just during those specific times I mentioned. Otherwise, I'm... I just feel regular, I guess.
Have you been avoiding any places or activities since the incident with your client?
No, I don't think so. I mean... I still go to work and do what I need to do. I haven't really stopped going anywhere.
Have these experiences been causing you significant distress or interfering with your daily life?

Well... I suppose it has. Work is... it's been hard. I've missed a couple of client deadlines lately. And I've actually stopped seeing people at the office. I just... I don't really trust myself to handle the returns right now. Or to keep the workplace safe. So... yes. It's interfering.
Are there any specific situations or reminders of the incident with your client that you've been trying to avoid?
No... I don't think so. Just... what I just said, about not seeing people in person right now. But as far as specific reminders... no. Not really.
Do you ever feel like you're on autopilot or going through the motions when you're not having one of those unreal moments?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I'm just trying to get my work done. I wouldn't really call it autopilot... I haven't noticed feeling like that.
Have you been feeling like you're observing yourself from outside your body at any times other than those 'unreal moments' you mentioned?
No... I haven't felt anything like that. I don't think I've ever felt like I was outside my body. Just... just the things I already told you about.
Are there any activities or situations that you've been avoiding because they remind you of the incident with your client?
I mean... I think I just mentioned this a minute ago. No. Just... not seeing clients in the office. There isn't anything else I'm avoiding.
Are there any specific things, such as sights, sounds, or smells, that remind you of the incident with your client and cause you distress?
No... not really. I mean, I haven't noticed anything like that. Just... I just try to keep my head down and work. I don't think there are specific sights or sounds or whatever.
Are there any emotions or physical sensations you experience when you think about the incident with your client?
I don't... I don't really know. I haven't been paying attention to that. I just try not to think about it at all, to be honest.
Are there any places or situations that you're avoiding because they remind you of the client who threatened you?
I... look, I thought we just went over this. It's just seeing people at the office. I'm not... I don't really go out much anyway right now. Just home. So, no. Nowhere else.
Have you been avoiding talking or thinking about the incident with your client?
I don't know if I'd call it avoiding. I just... there's really no reason to talk about it. It happened, and... I just want to focus on my work. That's all.
Are there any activities or things you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing since the incident with your client?

I don't know... I haven't really been doing much. My wife tries to joke with me, or she brings up going fishing like we had planned. I know those things are supposed to feel good, but... I don't know. It's just like the part of me that enjoys them has been switched off.
Have you been trying not to think about the incident with your client?
I don't know. I'm not... forcing myself to block it out, if that's what you mean. I just try to keep busy. That's it.
Have you lost interest in things you used to find enjoyable since the incident with your client?
Like I just said... with the fishing and everything. I just haven't really had the interest to do much of anything lately.
